transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-04 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Samira Gomez (Redwood SE), Michael Kwan (Venturi SRE), Priya Rao (Venturi Platform), Daniel Ortiz (Venturi Product)
Links shared: deck: https://redwood.example.com/deck/venturi-heatmap , bench sheet: https://redwood.example.com/bench/venturi-heatmap-spreadsheet

Summary (auto): Quick run of new correlation heatmap view in Console, followed by a scenario: high-latency spikes on chat-generation endpoint and buffered KV cache misses causing downstream error cascades. Discussed handoff steps for oncall and how to export heatmaps for postmortem.

[00:00:10] Jordan: ok great uh thanks everyone for joining, um today Samira and I will walk through the correlation heatmap in the Console and how you can use request logs to speed incident handoff. Michael can you give a quick context on where you saw the issue?
[00:00:25] Michael: yeah sure, we noticed intermittent 600ms spikes on our /v1/generate chat endpoint, user-facing latency spinner, sometimes followed by a 503 from our proxy, uh it's been cropping up after a deploy but not consistently.
[00:00:40] Priya: timeline wise we have a canary only for two epoches— I mean two hours— so it's been tricky to catch. Our stack is k8s on-prem (some nodes on aws peering) and we keep logs in ELK. We're interested in anything that stitches request id across Redwood calls.
[00:01:02] Samira: perfect, that maps well. The Console correlation heatmap ties request-level traces to token hops and KV cache hits/misses — so you can see patterns across concurrent requests. We'll demo a live session with a synthetic replay to show the spike.
[00:01:20] Jordan: quick qual — what's the retention requirement for you on logs and traces? and any strict PII rules we should watch for?
[00:01:28] Daniel: regulatory is moderate for our patient data team, we need SOC2 and also prefer customer-managed KMS for any private deployment. For hosted we'd need limited retention and strict redaction.
[00:01:40] Jordan: noted, we have both hosted with short retention and Private with KMS/HSM options. we'll include SOC2 docs after the call.
[00:01:50] ----- demo start -----
[00:02:05] Samira: ok pulling up the Console, this is the correlation heatmap view. columns are request bins by time, rows are correlated events: model invocations, prefix cache, kv cache eviction, network retry, and fallback hits. each cell has a density score and you can zoom in on a single request id.
[00:02:35] [00:02:40] Michael: hm the UI looks neat, how do you correlate our internal request id with your trace id?
[00:02:48] Samira: we accept an incoming header like x-venturi-request-id and we stitch it into our trace. if you can't send that header we try to map by client ip + timestamp heuristics, which is less accurate — that's where some transcription artefacts show up.
[00:03:06] Priya: is that mapping realtime or post-processing?
[00:03:10] Samira: realtime for the streaming traces; for heavy replays we do a short post-process pass to synthesize the heatmap. the heatmap refresh interval is configurable — default 30s.
[00:03:25] [00:03:30] Jordan: show the incident scenario we mocked?
[00:03:32] Samira: yep. replaying a 10-minute batch now — you can see a band of spikes at 14:12 where multiple requests have increased token latency. click on one.
[00:03:48] [00:03:50] Samira: this request shows a sequence: client -> inference front proxy -> model v2.1 -> kv cache miss -> long tail retry -> fallback to smaller model variant. the heatmap highlights a correlated cluster where kv cache miss ratio jumps from 5% to 42% in a 60s window.
[00:04:12] Michael: that kv cache number is interesting. we thought our prefix cache would have prevented it but maybe our sharding is off.
[00:04:20] Samira: right, and the Console overlays cost impact too — see the token-cost delta from the fallback. lower model variant saved latency but increased token count due to extra completion length in that particular prompt.
[00:04:33] Daniel: wait, so fallback helped latency but costs went up?
[00:04:36] Samira: in this example yes: fallback reduced wall time but required a two-stage call pattern which added token units overall. you can tune routing policies to prefer latency or cost.
[00:04:48] [00:04:55] Priya: how do we surface this to oncall? do you have a handoff export?
[00:05:00] Samira: yes there's an incident package export — it bundles the heatmap slice, top N request logs, stack traces, and a suggested runbook. you can email to your oncall channel or integrate with PagerDuty via webhook.
[00:05:12] Jordan: here's a sample export we prepared for Venturi (sending link)
[00:05:16] [00:05:20] Jordan: (link posted) Venturi-incident-package-heatmap-20260504.json
[00:05:25] Michael: great, that will help. question on data residency: if we run Dedicated or Private, do logs ever leave our VPC?
[00:05:34] Jordan: with Private the control plane can be customer-managed; logs and traces are stored in your VPC and we can optionally integrate with your KMS. for Dedicated (Redwood-managed) logs are in a tenant-isolated store in our region, and we provide audit logs and SOC2 artifacts.
[00:05:50] Priya: and SSO? we use SAML via Okta and have RBAC scoping.
[00:05:55] Samira: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; RBAC in Console lets you restrict who can export incident packages.
[00:06:05] [00:06:10] Daniel: latency SLOs — if we pick the hosted model with autoscaling, how predictable is p95 under load?
[00:06:18] Samira: depends on batching; our runtime tries continuous batching but for low-latency endpoints we pin to minimal batching and cold-start avoidance. we also have an autoscale warm pool in Dedicated that improves p95 consistency. typical p95 figures are in the deck but we'll share the specific profiles for your request-size distribution.
[00:06:40] Michael: can you show the logs for that specific request id?
[00:06:44] Samira: expanding the request timeline you can see timestamped events. note transcription sometimes shows k v cache as 'k v' — the underlying field name is kv_cache_hit. here's the http headers we saw and the model kernel selection: aten conv optimization — sorry micro-libs sometimes show as 'A T E N' in the transcript.
[00:07:08] [00:07:12] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[00:07:15] Samira: back to the heatmap, you can filter by error codes, by latency bucket, or by model variant. you can also tag runs so the postmortem links to the deploy id.
[00:07:28] Priya: do you keep a continuous archive for postmortem beyond 30 days? our compliance may need 90 days.
[00:07:34] Jordan: retention tiers are configurable; longer retention is an add-on in Hosted, included in Private if you host the storage. we will send the retention options in the follow-up.
[00:07:44] [00:07:50] Michael: curious about cost estimates for running the heavy tracing. how expensive is the heatmap telemetry?
[00:07:55] Samira: telemetry is sampled by default; full request capture is more expensive but for replay windows it's practical. in Optimize we provide suggestions: e.g. lower sampling to 1% with burst capture on anomalies; that keeps costs down while preserving fidelity for incidents.
[00:08:15] Daniel: are there competitor caveats — we tried another vendor and their trace stitching dropped request ids when proxies rewrite headers.
[00:08:22] Samira: we account for that with a four-way matching heuristic (header, ip, timestamp, and client id). it's not perfect but it's better than pure heuristics. also recommend instrumenting a persistent request id header from the app.
[00:08:36] [00:08:40] Jordan: ok let's run through the handoff script — Samira?
[00:08:43] Samira: step one: mark the incident slice in Console; step two: trigger incident export to oncall; step three: optionally kick a replay to reproduce the spike; step four: attach suggested remediation which often is TTL tuning on prefix cache or changing routing policy to avoid fallback.
[00:09:03] Michael: in our case we suspect prefix shard hotness after a few promos, would replay help?
[00:09:08] Samira: yes. replay will show if a small set of prompts are causing excessive token expansions or kv lookup storms. we can also run a replay under a dedicated capacity to see raw latencies without cross-tenant noise.
[00:09:22] Priya: what's the timeline to run a benchmark? we can give you logs by EOD tomorrow.
[00:09:27] Jordan: if you send a sanitized sample tomorrow we'll aim for a 48-hour replay run and share the heatmap and cost delta by May 7.
[00:09:35] [00:09:40] Daniel: any security review we should prep for?
[00:09:43] Jordan: we'll include SOC2, PCI is not in our standard pack but we can discuss. also include network diagram for VPC peering / private link when we schedule the infra deep dive.
[00:09:55] Samira: one more demo note — the Console has a 'timeline pin' feature. you can pin multiple request ids and then generate a unified report which we saw helped other health customers during oncall handoffs.
[00:10:10] Michael: nice. can that be exported as PDF or raw JSON?
[00:10:13] Samira: both. JSON for automation, PDF for postmortem decks.
[00:10:20] [00:10:26] Jordan: okay wrapping up, quick recap and next steps. Samira will produce a short runbook and export template; I'll send the correlation-heatmap deck and bench sheet; Venturi will share sanitized logs; we'll schedule the VPC/private deep dive next week.
[00:10:45] Priya: sounds good. thanks all.
[00:10:48] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with links and schedule invites.
[00:10:55] [00:11:00] End meeting
